aiSummary: Returning from a journey to Ha-noi and Chapa with colleagues from the Bureau, the author reflects on the unpredictability of resuming operations after travel, noting prior unfamiliarity with the region beyond official summaries and missionary reports. Initially reluctant due to casual acquaintance with the group and unsettling information from a colleague about their dealings, the author resolves to remain neutral despite growing unease. The journey began in Ha-noi, where the cold, fog-filled atmosphere contrasted sharply with the imagined tropical heat, and continued northwest toward Lao-kay after a delayed train, during which the author slept most of the time. Arriving in Lao-kay after a long ascent, the air grew sharper as the group moved to Chapa, where the landscape and atmosphere shifted, revealing an estrangement between upland and lowland communities influenced by French presence. The hotel, perched on a ridge, offered views of dark pines and shifting fog.
title: v2 tonkin
